title: Budget, monitoring and what lasts after the grant
course_title: Proposal Writing: Grants and Business Proposals

say: Budget, monitoring, and what lasts after the grant.
This is the video for module three of Proposal Writing.
The budget is your proposal written in numbers. Too high looks wasteful. Too low suggests you do not understand the work.

panel.heading: Every budget line shows
items: The unit: day, month, person, piece

say: Each line shows the item, the unit, the quantity and the unit cost. For example, 2 trainers, for 12 days, at 25,000 naira per day.

panel.heading: Every budget line shows
items: The unit: day, month, person, piece

say: The total is quantity times unit cost: 600,000 naira. Group your lines into categories, and always use the funder's template if it gives one.

say: For example, Amaka prices every line from 2 or 3 market quotes in Lafia. The course figures are illustrative and approximate.
Personnel, a part-time coordinator and two trainers: 1,200,000 naira.
Materials, including 40 starter kits and safety gear: 1,320,000 naira.
Venue, transport and refreshments: 1,440,000 naira.
Business support, 290,000 naira, and monitoring and evaluation, 250,000 naira.
Direct costs come to 4,500,000 naira. Administration at 7%, within the call's cap, adds 315,000 naira. Her request is 4,815,000 naira, under the 5,000,000 maximum.
Direct costs are spent only on this project.

cards.d: Spent only on this project, such as trainers' fees, materials and venue hire.
Shared running costs like bookkeeping and internet. Never exceed the call's cap.
What you give without asking the funder, like a free storage room. Show its value.

say: Indirect costs are your shared running costs. Many funders allow them only up to a stated percentage. Never exceed it.

say: In-kind contributions are things you provide yourself. Amaka's cooperative gives a storage room worth 180,000 naira. Show it in a separate column, because it proves commitment.
And leave ineligible costs, like vehicles, out completely.

say: Budget notes explain each line in one to three sentences. For example: 1,000 naira per woman per training day covers a return fare. Without it, the poorest members could not attend.

say: Monitoring tracks activities and outputs while the project runs. Evaluation judges whether outcomes were achieved. Every indicator needs a baseline, a target, a data source, a timing and a responsible person.

panel.heading: Amaka's month 4 check
items: Pattern: distant women, no regular buyers

say: At the end of month 4, Amaka's sales records show 22 of 40 women selling at least twice a month. Her target is 30.

panel.heading: Amaka's month 4 check
items: Pattern: distant women, no regular buyers

say: She looks for a pattern. Most of the women not selling live far from the market and have no regular buyers.

panel.heading: Amaka's month 4 check
items: Pattern: distant women, no regular buyers

say: So she pairs women to sell together at the weekly market, and introduces 3 school bursars to the group. By month 5, 27 sell regularly.

panel.heading: Amaka's month 4 check
items: Pattern: distant women, no regular buyers

say: By month 6, 31 of 40 sell regularly, above target. Her report states the low figure, the reason, the change and the result.

panel.rule: Report problems honestly. Funders value learning.

say: Sustainability means explaining which benefits last after the money ends, and how. The state government will take over is weak, unless you have a letter saying so.
Amaka gives concrete mechanisms. The cooperative will charge members 5,000 naira per place for a second training, as agreed at its general meeting. 6 of the strongest women become peer trainers.
Each woman saves 500 naira from every 5,000 naira of sales to buy her next batch, and links with 3 schools create regular buyers.
Claiming no risks looks naive. List what could go wrong, how likely and how serious it is, and your response.
Because her training uses caustic soda, Amaka plans for chemical burns: safety gear for every woman, a lye safety demonstration first, and a first aid kit and clean water at every session.
She also buys materials in bulk in month 1, and agrees the schedule with participants to avoid busy farming and festive weeks.

panel.heading: Amaka's risk responses
items: Chemical burn: safety gear for everyone
First aid kit and clean water every session
Price rises: buy materials in bulk in month 1
Low attendance: agree the schedule first

say: Your practice. Build your budget in a spreadsheet, with real quotes and notes for your biggest lines. Draft your M&E plan table. Write at least three sustainability mechanisms and a risk table.
Then score your draft against the funder's criteria. Now continue with the lessons below.
